title: The env-file rule does not refuse a heredoc whose prose names a sample env file while editing the env guard
why: Lane notes-fix-large-1 (session_013NEJL4DPEKRiC91yHkQV7m), 15:25 CST Nov 8, possible false alarm: the env-file rule refused a builder's Bash heredoc that edited hooks/guard_env.py. The heredoc read no file; a docstring and a comment named a sample env file name (an env stem with a .py suffix) as an example. Cost: a builder on the env guard cannot write prose about the names it matches. Step env-heredoc-false-alarm (done) covered heredoc text that only writes a file, so either this form escapes it or it regressed: reproduce first. Fix shape: ignore env names inside a heredoc body written to a file under hooks/, or list the case under the decision's Known false alarms.
note: Owner item 449 a (page answer 18:39 CST Nov 8): #2315 gets new commits and fresh review rounds 1 to 3 (coordinator 18:40 CST: it stays the PR, not closed) that add two narrowings: match the interpreter only as the heredoc's command word, and stop blanking after a nested backtick. 21:09 CST Nov 8: #2315 round 3 (reviewer sonnet) found it slightly net negative; held and parked. Owner page item 455 env-heredoc-net-negative (keep, drop, narrow); the answer goes to lane session_013NEJL1cp45E4ttwFy1ngig. Owner pick on the waiting page (13:09 CST Nov 9): item 455 a, with the note "record the gap". #2315 goes on to merge as it is, and its decision records the rare forms it lets through as a known gap. The owner chose it although it carries the label "Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo", so the pick is the owner's word for this act only.
